subject: Packaging sprint: pilot credits, batching/cache guidance, and quantization asks
messages:

Subject: Pilot ask — batching/caching/quant guidance + packaging question

Hi Sofia + Connor,

Thanks again for the demo last week. FastPay is keen to run a short pilot that tests latency improvements and cost delta if we adopt Redwood's batching + KV prefix caching and try an int8 quantized runtime path. Before we kick off, a couple quick asks:

- Do you have a recommended quantization path for our transformer stack (we're on a 7B variant)? Any known accuracy delta ranges you expect for int8 vs float16 on retrieval-augmented prompts?
- For packaging: what pilot credit would you recommend for a 4-week POC that covers 100k monthly inference tokens (spiky but bursty during business hours) plus a small embedding workload?
- Can you share a short mutual action plan template and any procurement docs we should prepare?

Attached: FastPay_telemetry_sample.csv (sample of request size/seq-length distribution).

Goal is to get a quick econ+tech alignment by early next week so we can author the SOW.

Thanks,
Bryan
Director, ML Platforms
FastPay Inc.

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Bryan Chen <bryan@fastpay.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot ask — batching/caching/quant guidance + packaging question

Thanks Bryan — great to see the telemetry. High level answers up front, then a short proposed plan below.

High-level:
- Quantization: for a 7B family model we typically recommend a staged path: int8-aware quantization for logits + KV paths (safest) and float16 inference for attention-heavy slices. Expect ~5-8% quality delta on tail-case prompts for purely int8 pipelines — most customers see negligible impact on LLM completions for user-facing templates after a small calibration run.
- Batching + KV caching: Given the bursty traffic, a combination of small continuous batching (50–200ms window) plus prefix KV caching for repeated conversational prefixes should reduce token cost by ~18–30% in our experience.
- Packaging/credits: For a 4-week POC at your volume we typically offer a pilot bucket that covers 120k equivalent inference tokens + 50k embedding units and a set number of reserved vCPU/GPU-hours for integration testing. We can either 1) apply a credit against usage (recommended for speed) or 2) create a short term committed SKU with a nominal discount.

Proposed mutual action plan (short):
1) Week 0 (this week): align on telemetry and success metrics (latency p95, cost per 1k tokens, quality regression tolerance).
2) Week 1: provisioning + lightweight integration (redwood sandbox, keys, KV cache policy).
3) Week 2–3: run canonical traffic, collect metrics, run small A/B on int8 vs float16 with a shared prompt set.
4) Week 4: results review and decision point (roll to dedicated or iterate).

I've attached a one-page sprint proposal (2026-09-30-redwood-sprint-proposal-v1.pdf) and a short KV sizing sheet — can you confirm whether the sample telemetry covers ~2 weeks of peak-hours? If so, Connor can produce a rough credit estimate and a sizing-based credit recommendation by EOD tomorrow.

Would you prefer credits applied to the hosted API usage or to a short-term Dedicated reservation for the POC? Credits are faster; Dedicated reservation gives you predictable latency if that's a concern.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Bryan Chen <bryan@fastpay.ai>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot ask — batching/caching/quant guidance + packaging question

Bryan — quick technical follow-up and a draft econ suggestion below.

On quantization and quality:
- For your 7B stack we recommend running two comparators in the POC: (A) baseline float16 inference, (B) int8 quantized path with per-layer calibration (we'll provide tooling). Expect 0–7% delta on open-completion metrics; regression is concentrated on low-frequency tokens and long-tail completions. We'll include an eval harness to quantify µ/σ across your prompt suite.

On batching + KV cache config:
- Continuous batching window: start conservative at 75ms and tune to 150ms if latency SLO allows.
- KV cache policy: cache 3 most-recent conversation prefixes per user for 24–48 hours; we can adjust TTL based on hit-rate during the first run.

Econ/packaging draft (based on telemetry attached):
- Pilot credits (recommended): 120k inference-token credit + 50k embedding credits + 30 GPU-minutes of dedicated-seat validation for integration (applied as credit to hosted usage).
- Accelerated option: 1-week Dedicated reservation (small) + 30% pilot credit applied to baseline usage for the test window (useful if p95 latency matters).
- Discount ask: for a first pilot we can offer a one-time 15% pilot credit on consumption beyond the free bucket for the 4-week window; for a follow-up committed contract (6–12 months) we can discuss tiered credits up to 30% based on committed tokens.

Attachments: kv-cache-sizing-sheet.xlsx (simple sizing model).

If those options look good I can put together a short SOW + credit statement for procurement. Also looping Marcus for billing/legal redlines and Mina for success metrics instrumentation.

Cheers,
Connor O'Brien
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
